title: Fallback routing debug logbook
content:
Personal scratchpad / breadcrumbs for the smart routing + fallback incident (notes to self).

---
Context:
- Incident window: 2026-01-08 22:10-22:45 UTC (observed).
- Symptom: a subset of production traffic pinned to us-west1 started getting ModelUnavailable/503s; automatic fallback to eu-central1 happened but some requests still returned 503s or timed out.
- Affected: hosted-api routes using model gptx-3b-v1 + dedicated-backed model variants.

What I saw (first-pass):
- Alerts triggered from routing SLO dashboard: spike in route-level 5xx and p95 latency for route /v1/chat/gptx (us-west1).
- Router logs show repeated "no compatible variant" and then fallback attempts. Some fallbacks succeeded, some failed with different error.

Timestamps & snippets (copied from pods / logs):
- 2026-01-08T22:12:03Z smart-router-1 ERROR "route select failed: no healthy backends for model=gptx-3b-v1@us-west1"
- 2026-01-08T22:12:04Z smart-router-1 INFO "fallback_policy: region_failover -> candidate eu-central1; initiating IPC to mux-bridge"
- 2026-01-08T22:12:04Z mux-bridge WARN "connect timeout to eu-central1 gateway (1200ms), retrying once"
- 2026-01-08T22:12:05Z smart-router-1 ERROR "fallback failed: RouteError(code=BackendConnectionFailed, msg=\"tls handshake timeout\")"
- 2026-01-08T22:12:07Z smart-router-1 INFO "fallback succeeded to eu-central1 after 2 attempts (latency penalty +85ms)"
- 2026-01-08T22:13:11Z smart-router-1 ERROR "fallback_policy: backup_variant unavailable: ModelUnavailableError(capacity_quota_exceeded)"
- 2026-01-08T22:14:55Z smart-router-1 ERROR "request timed out after 30000ms while waiting for kv-cache warmup"

Commands I ran (local and on cluster):
- curl test from laptop (simulating region header):
  curl -sS -D - -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'X-Region-Hint: us-west1' \  -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat \  -d '{"model":"gptx-3b-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'
  -> got 503 + body: {"error":"ModelUnavailableError","detail":"no healthy backends"}

- kubectl logs smart-router-1 -n prod --since=30m | grep -i fallback > /tmp/fallbacks.txt
- kubectl exec -it smart-router-1 -n prod -- curl -s localhost:9090/health | jq . -> ok
- kubectl exec -it mux-bridge-0 -n prod -- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/backends | jq '.[] | select(.region=="eu-central1")'
  -> some backends flagged unhealthy with last_healthcheck=2026-01-08T22:11:00Z

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
1) Upstream capacity/exhaustion: dedicated pools in us-west1 hit a quota spike; router correctly attempts region failover. Some eu-central backends were flaky (healthchecks failing) -> partial fallbacks.
2) TLS handshake timeouts indicate either transient network flaps between clusters or overloaded gateway proxies in eu-central1. Could be cloud-provider networking (GCP inter-region routes).
3) KV cache cold/warm interactions: when fallback to eu-central, requests need to build KV caches; if KV warmups exceed route timeout we get timeouts. Observed "kv-cache warmup" timeouts. Implication: fallback should avoid synchronous KV warmups (or use cached prefixes).
4) Route policy misconfiguration: fallback weights / max_concurrent_fallbacks not set; we attempted too many simultaneous cross-region fallbacks and tripped connection pools.
5) LB / healthcheck flakiness: some backends failing healthchecks due to ephemeral load spikes; during the health window router saw them as unhealthy then later healthy -> flapping.

What I changed / tried (and results):
- Short-term: temporarily disabled region_failover for the route to prevent cross-region thrash (config change) -> reduced error noise but increased original 5xx for affected users (expected).
- Replayed synthetic traffic (small qps) with header X-Region-Hint forcing eu-central1 -> eu-central responded OK for low qps, but at scale connection timeouts reappeared.
- Increased router->gateway connect timeout from 1000ms -> 2000ms for eu-central1 to see if TLS handshake timeouts reduce -> observed fewer handshake timeouts but p95 latency rose ~20ms.
- Evicted local KV cache entries on a few backend nodes (kubectl exec ...) to force rewarm and measured warmup times ~400-800ms per warmup; at scale this adds up.

Errors seen (raw-ish):
- {"time":"2026-01-08T22:12:05Z","level":"error","msg":"BackendConnectionFailed","region":"eu-central1","err":"TLS handshake timeout after 1200ms"}
- {"time":"2026-01-08T22:14:55Z","level":"error","msg":"KVWarmupTimeout","route":"/v1/chat/gptx","timeout_ms":30000}

Open questions / next steps:
- Infra: Ask infra to check inter-region packet loss / BGP logs between us-west1 and eu-central1 for 22:10-22:20 UTC. (Arjun to ping GCP support).
- Capacity: Confirm dedicated pool usage graphs for us-west1 at that minute. Were there scheduled jobs, nightly batch, or unusual spikes? (Diego owns metrics).
- Routing config: Audit fallback_policy config for this route. Is max_parallel_fallbacks sane? Are we allowing too many cross-region TLS connections concurrently?
- KV strategy: Explore asynchronous KV warmup or returning a partial response while warming sync in background. Add telemetry: count of requests requiring cross-region kv-warmups and warmup latency distribution.
- Healthchecks: Increase frequency to catch flaps? Or add short cooldown before flipping to unhealthy. Need to balance detection vs noise.

Notes to self (stuff I don't want to forget):
- When reproducing, use small qps -> then ramp quickly to reveal the threshold where eu-central gateway times out. Measure socket-level timeouts (ss / netstat) on gateway hosts.
- Check gateway proxy JVM/HTTP client thread pool saturation metrics (connection pool exhaustion will look like handshake timeouts sometimes).
- If fallback is common, consider prefer-local-variant policy that can fallback to a quantized/less-capable variant in same region before region failover.
- Remember to snapshot router config before any change: curl -s https://config-api/.../routes/gptx -> save diff.

Decision log (short):
- 2026-01-08 23:00 UTC: rollbacked temporary routing disable after small config tweak -> left region_failover enabled but with max_parallel_fallbacks=5 and increased connection timeout for eu-central TLS.
- 2026-01-10 10:23 UTC: infra confirmed packet loss spike between regions at 22:11 UTC; relieved (likely root cause). Follow-up tasks scheduled to harden retries and add async kv-warmup.

Reminder: This is a personal scratch doc — not polished. Copy relevant snippets to the incident postmortem and to JIRA ticket (JIRA-INC-2026-412) where we will consolidate and assign owners.

Possible long-term mitigations (brainstorm):
- Prefer-local fallback variant (quantized) before region failover.
- Warm standby prefix caching in non-primary regions for top-k models to reduce kv-warmup latency on failover.
- Circuit-breaker on cross-region fallback using token-bucket to limit parallel cross-region requests and avoid gateway saturation.
- Better telemetry: per-request flag whether fallback happened + kv-warmup latency and backend selection chain.

End of scratchpad.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add async kv-warmup experiment to canary (owner: me)
- [ ] Follow up with Diego on pool usage graphs (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Infra check with GCP (owner: Arjun)
- [ ] Add per-request fallback telemetry (owner: eng-observability)

---
